data.long_meaning: The name Karissa is derived from the Greek word kários, which means pure, clear, and precious. In the Bible, there is no character named Karissa. in_hebrew.name: קאריסה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם קאריסה נגזר מהמילה היוונית 'כאריס' שפירושה חן ורצון. בהקשר המקראי, השם מייצג את האהבה והקבלה של אלוהים. השם נמצא בשימוש נרחב בקרב הנוצרים כסמל לאהבת האל והחסד שלו.

in_greek.name: Καρίσσα
in_greek.meaning: Χάρις και αγάπη από τον Θεό
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Καρίσσα προέρχεται από το ελληνικό 'χάρις' που σημαίνει χάρη και αγάπη. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, η χάρις αναφέρεται στη θεία εύνοια και αγάπη. Ως εκ τούτου, το όνομα Καρίσσα συμβολίζει την αγάπη και το έλεος του Θεού.

in_latin.name: Karissa
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Karissa derivatur a verbo Graeco 'χάρις', quod gratiam et favorem significat. In ecclesia primitiva, nomen hoc usitatum erat ut symbolum amoris et misericordiae Dei. Karissa igitur est nomen quod amorem et gratiam divinam repraesentat.

in_english.name: Karissa
in_english.meaning: Beloved, dear one, or cherished by God
in_english.long_meaning: The name Karissa originates from the Greek word 'χάρις' (charis), meaning grace, favor, or love. Although not directly mentioned in the Bible, the name embodies the biblical concept of divine love and grace. Historically, the name has been used in Christian traditions to signify a child cherished and loved by God. It symbolizes spiritual blessings, love, and divine favor.

data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Karissa is derived from the Greek word 'karis' which means grace. In Christian tradition, this name symbolizes the divine gift of God's grace bestowed upon an individual. It is a reminder of God's infinite love and favor towards us.

biblical_reference.note: Though not directly found in the Bible, the root 'charis' appears frequently, emphasizing God's grace.

historical_references.reference: In the 16th century, there was a popular Latin hymn called 'Caritas Christi Urget' which contained the line 'Karissimus Iesu Redemptor' meaning 'Dearest Jesus, Redeemer'. This is likely one of the earliest recorded uses of the name Karissa in a Christian context.

In the 18th century, a French girl named Marie-Anne Angélique de Tarn, also known as 'the Little Flower of Jesus', reportedly received a vision in which she was given the name 'Karissimme' by Jesus. Though the spelling varies, this is another important Christian reference to the name Karissa.
